description: The bettermemory 9 store's hash-chained log. `log verify` checks every row's MAC against the key kept outside the store, the chain between rows, the head checkpoint against the last row, the origin anchor against the row where this host's history begins, and every table against a replay of the log. Exit 0 when the log verifies, 1 when it is tampered or cannot be verified. `log export` writes the log as JSON Lines for an audit pipeline, `log anchor` takes an anchor to keep off this host for `log verify --anchor`, and `log accept-history` accepts a replaced history on the record.
log: Verify the log: MACs, chain, head, the origin anchor and fold, and every --anchor given. The origin anchor, kept beside the key outside the store (<store_id>.origin in the keys directory), names the row where this host's history of the store begins and the key that signed it: that row must still be in the log with the same MAC and verify under that key. A row gone or changed, or one that key does not verify while it is still held here, adds the problem origin_mismatch and the log reads tampered. When that key is no longer held (its key file was lost) or no key is held at all, nothing here can check the row: the origin reads unverifiable, and so does the log, until the key is filed back (`bettermemory key import`). `bettermemory log accept-history --yes` accepts a replaced history on purpose, on the record. Prints a report and exits 0 only when every check passes; 1 when the log is tampered or cannot be verified (an anchor or an origin that no longer matches is tampering); 2 when there is no store or an anchor file cannot be read.

Write the log as JSON Lines, one object per row in seq order, for a SIEM or an audit archive: seq, ts, kind, class, session, actor, record ids, the payload, the MAC and the MAC it chains to, the segment's key fingerprint and whether the row's MAC verifies under the key held here (null when it is not held). Bodies and other free text are replaced by their sha256 and length unless --include-bodies. Read-only and deterministic: the same log gives the same bytes. Exit 0 when the export is written, 1 when the output closed before it was, 2 when there is no store it can read, an argument is wrong or --out cannot be written (or names the store's own files or the keys directory). The export is a trail, not a verdict: run `log verify` for that.

Take an anchor of the log: the store id, the last row's seq and MAC, a SHA-256 over every row's MAC up to it, and the time. Keep it off this host (a ticket, a git repository, a WORM bucket); `log verify --anchor FILE` then shows whether history up to that seq was rewritten since, even by a process that holds the key. Prints the anchor as one JSON line, or writes it to --out. Exit 0 when the anchor is taken, 2 when there is no store it can read, its log is empty or --out cannot be written (or names the store's own files or the keys directory).

Accept the store file's history as it stands, on the record, when the origin anchor reads origin_mismatch or unverifiable or the head checkpoint names a row the log does not hold: a store file copied over this host's copy again, an anchor from before 9.0.0rc13 whose key was lost, an older copy put back by hand. With the daemon stopped, the key ring is bound to this file and the store opened as its owner opens it (a missing or foreign key is settled as any writing command settles it); a history_accepted row, signed with the store's key, names the anchor, head and binding before and after; then this host's history is anchored at the first row of the earliest segment a key it holds signs and the head moved to the row, so a crash leaves the acceptance recorded or none; last the rewind record beside the head (<store_id>.backup_restore.json) gets the same entry. Refused while a daemon serves or starts for the store, or when the key file cannot be read. Without --yes prints the plan. Exit 0 accepted (or nothing to accept), 1 refused, failed or the log still tampered after it, 2 no store, 3 the plan.
root: health
Print the aggregate memory health report.
init
Onboard a fresh install: print the MCP config snippet, or auto-patch a known client's config. Idempotent.
migrate
One-shot data migrations. `migrate v8` reads a v8 store directory into a bettermemory 9 store.
export

Dump all active memories (and tombstones, by default) to a self-describing JSON document, with each record's home, for reading or for an external indexer. It is not a backup: it leaves out the signed log, episodes, conflicts and the other tables, and no command restores a store from it. `bettermemory backup create` makes a backup. Writes to stdout unless --output is given.
tombstones
Inspect, restore, and prune the tombstone (removed-memory) audit log. Subcommands: list, restore, prune.
rollback
Remove the memories one actor wrote, leaving every other actor's in place. Dry-run by default; --apply --yes commits. Every removal is a tombstone, so `tombstones restore` puts a record back.
episodes
Inspect and prune the episode (journal) store — the sibling-to-memory tier for loop-iteration takeaways. Subcommands: list, prune.
log

The bettermemory 9 store's hash-chained log. `log verify` checks every row's MAC against the key kept outside the store, the chain between rows, the head checkpoint against the last row, the origin anchor against the row where this host's history begins, and every table against a replay of the log. Exit 0 when the log verifies, 1 when it is tampered or cannot be verified. `log export` writes the log as JSON Lines for an audit pipeline, `log anchor` takes an anchor to keep off this host for `log verify --anchor`, and `log accept-history` accepts a replaced history on the record.
index

The store's full-text search index. `index rebuild` spells every memory's index text again from its body and scopes and rebuilds the FTS5 table from it, the repair doctor and backup verify name for an index drift.
key

The store's key ring: the key outside the store that signs its log, the retired keys earlier segments verify under, the head checkpoint, the origin anchor and the binding to one store file. `key show` reads it; `key export` and `key import` keep and file back keys; `key adopt` binds the ring to this store file; `key rotate` writes a new key. Every change is a row in the store's log, signed with its key. No key file is placed or deleted by hand.
project
The projects membership knows (list, show, why, pending, folder) and the declarations that settle a checkout's project (join, new, init).
memory
One record at a time. `memory move` re-homes a record to another project (or global); `memory history` lists every log row that made, changed or removed it.
membership
Membership across stores: export the projects' portable identities and the records' homes, import them into this store, and migrate a store's records into projects.
eval
Compute the three memory-effectiveness rates (memory_helped_rate, endorsement_rate, silent_miss_rate) from the event log + active store. Methodology in docs/eval.md.
review

The write review's grading surface. `review samples` draws reviewed writes from a window and shows each one's related set, answers and action; `review grade` records the owner's grade of one as a review_grade event, which `bettermemory eval` counts.
capture

Session capture's batches. `capture review` lists each batch with its outcome, how many memories it saved, its refusals by rule and what was undone; `capture undo BATCH` tombstones a batch's memories (dry-run unless --apply); `capture sample` and `capture grade` draw captured memories and record the owner's grade of each against the ten rules. Calls no model.
recall

The recall surface's grading surface. `recall review` draws prompt recall deliveries, session briefs and silent prompts from a window and shows each one's pointers and the prompt it answered; `recall grade` records the owner's grade of a sample's pointers as a recall_grade event, which `bettermemory eval` counts.
rename-scope

Replace OLD with NEW across every memory's scope list — the cheap fix for a typo'd or deprecated scope (e.g. `infra` -> `infrastructure`). The CLI counterpart of memory_admin's rename_scope action. Bumps `updated` but preserves `last_verified_at`; tombstones are renamed too unless --no-tombstones.
try
Instant offline demo: watch a memory go stale when a file it cites moves.
backup

Verified backups of the bettermemory 9 store. `backup create` writes a consistent snapshot bundle while the daemon runs, `backup verify` checks a bundle's files, signature and log on a temporary copy, and `backup restore` puts one back with the daemon stopped, rewinding the head checkpoint on the record so `log verify` passes.
service

Run the local daemon as a supervised service: a launchd LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux, started at login and again after a crash. `install` writes and loads the unit, `uninstall` unloads and removes it, `status` reports it, `print` writes it to stdout only. Exit 2 on other platforms, with the command to supervise yourself, and when the config (config.toml or the managed file) does not load, with the loader's message.
doctor

Check the install, the config, the store and its key, the daemon, the client wiring, the disk and the key rings whose store is gone, read-only, each ok, warn or fail with a one-line fix. Exit 0 when every check is ok, 1 on any failure, 2 on warnings only. Posture (file modes, the sandbox) is `bettermemory security audit`'s.
security

Security checks for this install. `security audit` reports whether the store, the key and the daemon's files are as SECURITY.md assumes; `security sandbox` prints Claude Code sandbox settings for this host's paths; `security scan` finds credentials and chat-template control tokens kept in the store. None writes a row, a key or a file of its own.
stats

Usage and growth of the store, read-only: file sizes, rows per table, memories by project, scope, client, model and category, records created and removed and log rows written per day over the last DAYS days, tombstones, episodes, log rows by kind, and the oldest and newest records. Aggregate SQL only: no MAC is checked (`log verify` does that). Exit 0 with the report, 2 when no store is found or the config or the store file cannot be read.
completion

Print a completion script for bash, zsh or fish, generated from this build's own parser, so it completes every subcommand and flag this version has. Prints only; regenerate it after an upgrade. bash: add `eval "$(bettermemory completion bash)"` to ~/.bashrc. zsh: after compinit in ~/.zshrc, add `eval "$(bettermemory completion zsh)"`, or save the output as _bettermemory in a directory on $fpath. fish: `bettermemory completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/bettermemory.fish`.
config

Where the config lives (`config path`), the settings in force and where each came from (`config show`), and the lines that do not do what they say (`config check`). Read-only: never creates the config file, the store or the keys.
up
Start the local daemon for this store, detached, or report the one already running. --foreground runs it in this process, for supervisors. Exit 0 when a daemon runs, 1 when none could be started.
down
Stop the local daemon for this store. Exit 0 when it stopped or was not running, 1 when it did not stop; its state file is then kept while its process holds the store's lock.
status

Report whether the local daemon for this store is running. Exit 0; with --check the exit code is the answer: 0 running and answering as this store's daemon, 1 not running, 2 a state file whose daemon does not answer but may be alive (it holds the store's lock), 3 the port answers, but not as this store's healthy daemon (another store or process, or a reply that is not a daemon's /health).
serve
Run the MCP server over stdio in this process, without the daemon. `bettermemory` with no arguments is the stdio shim in front of the daemon.
hook
Run a harness hook through the daemon: session-start, stop or prompt. Reads the hook's stdin JSON, prints the daemon's answer, always exits 0.

usage: bettermemory log [-h] {verify,export,anchor,accept-history} ...

where this host's history begins, and every table against a replay of the
log. Exit 0 when the log verifies, 1 when it is tampered or cannot be
verified. `log export` writes the log as JSON Lines for an audit pipeline,

--anchor`, and `log accept-history` accepts a replaced history on the
record.

  {verify,export,anchor,accept-history}
    verify              Verify the log: MACs, chain, head, the origin
                        anchor and fold, and every --anchor given. The
                        origin anchor, kept beside the key outside the
                        store (<store_id>.origin in the keys directory),
                        names the row where this host's history of the
                        store begins and the key that signed it: that row
                        must still be in the log with the same MAC and
                        verify under that key. A row gone or changed, or
                        one that key does not verify while it is still held
                        here, adds the problem origin_mismatch and the log
                        reads tampered. When that key is no longer held

                        nothing here can check the row: the origin reads
                        unverifiable, and so does the log, until the key is
                        filed back (`bettermemory key import`).

                        replaced history on purpose, on the record. Prints
                        a report and exits 0 only when every check passes;
                        1 when the log is tampered or cannot be verified
                        (an anchor or an origin that no longer matches is
                        tampering); 2 when there is no store or an anchor
                        file cannot be read.

                        seq order, for a SIEM or an audit archive: seq, ts,
                        kind, class, session, actor, record ids, the
                        payload, the MAC and the MAC it chains to, the
                        segment's key fingerprint and whether the row's MAC
                        verifies under the key held here (null when it is
                        not held). Bodies and other free text are replaced
                        by their sha256 and length unless --include-bodies.

                        files or the keys directory). The export is a
